Hasanbeigi, A., Arens, M. and Price, L. (2014). Alternative emerging ironmaking technologies for energy-efficiency and carbon dioxide emissions reduction: A technical review. Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews 33, 645-658. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2014.02.031

Review compiling other sources; nearly every number is reprinted (the reference is named in each note). Locators are journal pages. Main file: 16 technologies (conventional BF plus 12 alternative ironmaking processes, with Circored/Circofer split and suspension hydrogen reduction split by its three reductants), each with a description and the source's commercialization status (state-of-development; no TRL printed); BF energy range 13.0-14.1 GJ/t pig iron (Energetics 2004); cyclone converter furnace 13-14 GJ/thm; MOE 3,500 kWh/t molten steel; PSH furnace capex derived from $16,729,000 / 46,000 t/yr; reference-plant capacities for FINEX, ITmk3, coal-based HYL, MXCOL and Circored; CO2 reduction potentials versus a BF (COREX, PSH, suspension reduction, biomass RHF). _measures.csv: relative savings versus the BF or other routes (COREX fuel -18%, FINEX capex -20%/production cost -15%, ITmk3 -30%, PSH -30%, suspension -38% and 7.4 GJ/t, biomass RHF productivity +50%). _other-values.csv: pilot capacities, temperatures, process times, whole-route CO2 figures (MOE 345 and BF 1,750 kg CO2/t liquid steel include electricity or the whole route, so not scope-1 parameters), the 16.1 GJ/thm BF-with-coke-and-sinter benchmark and the 1.8 t CO2/t rolled coil plant figure. Not loaded: Table 1 feedstock/reductant matrix (qualitative), all qualitative benefit bullets. No flows file: no per-unit input quantities are printed. The same material, with more technologies, is in LBNL-6106E (hasanbeigi_2013_001).

(1) No original data: values are compiled from company claims and older studies (De Beer 1998, Birat 1990s, AISI roadmap). (2) No currency year for the PSH furnace cost ($16,729,000; engineering study commissioned 2006) and no statement of what it covers. (3) Sect. 3.2 (FINEX) introduces its benefit list as 'benefits reported for COREX compared to BF'. (4) Sect. 3.7 prints the reducing-gas temperature as '9,00 1C'. (5) Sect. 3 intro lists 'charging carbon composite agglomerates' but the paper has no section on it (only 12 technologies). (6) ITmk3 process time printed 0.15 h here but 10 minutes in the LBNL report. (7) MOE CO2 (345 kg/t) assumes 90 g CO2/kWh, which footnote 4 itself calls very low. (8) Energy figures give no heating-value basis and no carrier split. (9) Emissions reductions are against differing baselines (per t product, per t hot metal, 'BF process').
